They're not that perishable. I have 18 chickens and we get at least a dozen per day. I keep them for up to six months in the fridge w/o washing so they stay fresh, but there are ways to preserve them also. If you're interested go to YT and check out some videos.
I’ve read that wiping the fresh eggs down with mineral oil helps keep fresh eggs even longer.

We have laying chickens and when we get too many eggs, we freeze them. Use a muffin pan. Just put one or two eggs in each muffin cup and pop them out when they are frozen and put in a freezer bag. You can leave them whole or scramble them before you freeze them. You can even cook them over easy after thawing and you'd never know they were frozen. The silicone muffin pans are really nice because you can so easily pop them out. It seems like when I used to use the metal muffin pans that I sprayed them with grease first.
I do that too. I freeze the yolks and whites separately in ice cube trays. That way I'm able to add more egg white if need be.
